meta.title: Empirical Research Methods
meta.one_liner: Ask a question about people, design a survey, collect the data, and test it with regression.
meta.blurb: This course taught students to evaluate and run original research on human behavior. Each student picked a question about life in Qatar, wrote a proposal, completed human subjects training, went through IRB review, wrote and piloted a survey, and collected their own data. We covered measurement, scales, sampling, survey design, and experiments along the way, then spent the last weeks on analysis so that every final paper tested its main hypothesis with regression. The semester ended with three days of student research presentations.

assignments.name: Final research report
assignments.description: A 2,000 to 2,500 word paper with introduction, literature review of at least three research articles, hypotheses, methods, results, and the survey as an appendix. Every paper had to test its main hypothesis with regression.

assignments.name: Final presentation
assignments.description: A short talk on the study and its results, over three days at the end of the semester.

assignments.name: Pilot studies and drafts
assignments.description: CITI human subjects training, two proposal drafts, IRB forms, and a survey draft that classmates took and critiqued in class before the final version went out.

assignments.name: Two midterm exams
assignments.description: 20% each, on research design and measurement, then sampling, surveys, and experiments.

assignments.name: Online quizzes
assignments.description: Eight quizzes on the Babbie readings, lowest score dropped.

assignments.name: Participation
assignments.description: Attendance by clicker, and in-class design exercises.
